{"Author":"dajoey","Name":"LazyRetainerLive","Punchline":"Real-time retainer venture countdowns for your dashboard.","Description":"Serves the logged-in character's live retainer and venture state on loopback HTTP (127.0.0.1:10504) so the ffxiv dashboard relay can show real-time venture countdowns instead of AutoRetainer's occasionally-stale file cache.","InternalName":"LazyRetainerLive","AssemblyVersion":"0.0.0.0","TestingAssemblyVersion":"0.1.0.1","TestingDalamudApiLevel":15,"Changelog":"v0.1.0.1 (2026-09-05)


- Corrected a wrong claim in the v0.1.0.0 notes below (and on the mod's web page): **the endpoint does not answer 503 on logout.** Once logged in, it keeps serving that character's last known retainer state - including at the title screen - and only ever answers 503 if it has never read the retainer table at all since the plugin loaded (i.e. it started at the title screen and no login has happened yet). That freeze is deliberate and is the better behaviour: measured on 2026-09-05 the frozen live snapshot was still *newer* than AutoRetainer's file, so falling back to the file on logout would have shown the dashboard **older** data, not fresher. No behaviour was changed here - only the description was wrong (file: `HttpServer.cs`, `RetainerLiveService.cs`, `RetainerState.cs`).
- The settings window no longer reports "serving live snapshot" while logged out. It now distinguishes three states: no snapshot yet, serving a live snapshot, or serving the last-known snapshot while the game is in transition (file: `ConfigWindow.cs`, new `RetainerLiveService.LastTickOk`).


- For anything scripting against this endpoint: `readAt` is the time the request was **served**, not the time the data was read from the game, so it does not reveal how stale a frozen snapshot is. Use the settings window (or `/lazyretainerlive debug`) to tell live from frozen.

v0.1.0.0 (2026-09-05)


- First release. LazyRetainerLive reads the logged-in character's LIVE retainer table (the same in-memory data AutoRetainer uses to drive its own countdowns) and serves it as JSON on `http://127.0.0.1:10504/retainers`, so the ffxiv dashboard's retainer panel can show venture countdowns that update the moment a venture is collected instead of whenever AutoRetainer next saves its config file.
- When not logged in (or the live table has no data yet) the endpoint answers HTTP 503, which tells the dashboard relay to fall back to AutoRetainer's file. Loopback only - the port is never reachable from other machines.


- Companion of AutoRetainer - it reads, it never writes, assigns, or collects anything. Settings: Enabled (default on) and loopback port (default 10504). Commands: `/lazyretainerlive` opens settings, `/lazyretainerlive debug` dumps listener + snapshot state, `/lazyretainerlive changelog` reopens this popup.
- Why this exists: AutoRetainer's `DefaultConfig.json` (which feeds the dashboard today) is saved only at AutoRetainer's own save points, so its venture rows can be tens of minutes stale while ventures are actually completing. The countdown for the logged-in character lives in the game's memory - this plugin is a small read-only window onto it.","RepoUrl":"https://github.com/dajoey/lalalazy/tree/main/src/LazyRetainerLive","ApplicableVersion":"any","DalamudApiLevel":15,"IsHide":false,"IsTestingExclusive":true,"DownloadLinkInstall":"https://raw.githubusercontent.com/dajoey/lalalazy/main/plugins/LazyRetainerLive/latest/latest.zip","DownloadLinkUpdate":"https://raw.githubusercontent.com/dajoey/lalalazy/main/plugins/LazyRetainerLive/latest/latest.zip","DownloadLinkTesting":"https://raw.githubusercontent.com/dajoey/lalalazy/main/plugins/LazyRetainerLive/testing/testing.zip","Tags":["retainers","ventures","dashboard","http","lazy"],"CategoryTags":["utility"],"IconUrl":"https://raw.githubusercontent.com/dajoey/lalalazy/main/LalaImages/lazyretainerlive-icon.png","ImageUrls":[""],"DownloadCount":0,"LastUpdate":"0","_SourceId":"dajoey-lalalazy","_SourceName":"dajoey / lalalazy","_SourceUrl":"https://raw.githubusercontent.com/dajoey/lalalazy/main/pluginmaster.json"}

{"Author":"dajoey","Name":"LazyFashionReport","Punchline":"What to wear, what to dye, and what you'll score - before Masked Rose judges you.","Description":"Fashion Report assistant for the Gold Saucer: shows the week's hints, the exact +2 dye and +1 shade for each left-side slot, and top candidate items from the crowdsourced database filtered to what you actually own - with a live score predictor as you assemble the outfit.","InternalName":"LazyFashionReport","AssemblyVersion":"0.0.0.0","TestingAssemblyVersion":"0.1.1.0","TestingDalamudApiLevel":15,"Changelog":"v0.1.1.0 (2026-09-07)

- The window no longer shows a bare list of slots with "no hint" under every row. The weekly hint/theme/dye data comes from fashionreportxiv.com, whose payload is formatted differently than the plugin assumed; the data downloaded successfully but every field silently failed to be read, so the window looked half-built while the log said everything was fine. All fields now bind correctly, and when a data source fails to load the window says which one and why instead of showing an empty table (files: `Core/RemoteDataSource.cs`, `FashionService.cs`, `ReportWindow.cs`)
- A single unknown item id in the crowdsourced data no longer aborts the whole weekly rebuild. One junk id (1010533) threw while names were being looked up and took every hint, dye and candidate down with it; unknown ids now fall back to showing the raw item number (file: `Adapters/SheetAdapter.cs`, `WarmItemNames`)
- The settings window's data-status line now names each source separately instead of one combined "data loaded" that stayed green while the hint source had failed (file: `ConfigWindow.cs`)

- Verified offline against week 449's real downloaded payload (theme "Hunter from the Far East": four hints, six dye slots, base 70, the published easy-100 set scores exactly 100). The regression fixture replays the actual bytes from the live site through the same parsing path the plugin uses (file: `tests/LazyFashionReport.Harness`)
- If the window still says "MISSING" for a source, /lfr refresh re-downloads; cached data from earlier sessions is used when a download fails (file: `Core/RemoteDataSource.cs`)

v0.1.0.0 (2026-09-06)

- First testing release: a Fashion Report assistant for the Gold Saucer. Open the in-game Fashion Report window (or type /lfr) and LazyFashionReport shows, for every gear slot: the week's hint, the exact +2 dye and the +1 shade family for left-side slots, and the top candidate items from the crowdsourced database (xivstats) filtered down to items actually owned - bags, glamour dresser and armoire included (files: Core/ScoreMath.cs, Core/Predictor.cs, Adapters/CrowdDataAdapter.cs)
- A live score predictor: as the worn outfit changes, the window shows "scores N - needs +X for 80" per slot and in total, computed from the verified scoring rules (10/8 base per unhinted slot, hinted slots 2 + 8/6 for a correct item, exact dye +2 / same shade +1 on left-side slots) (file: Core/ScoreMath.cs SlotScore / WeeklyBase)
- The weekly base is computed from where the hints landed, never hardcoded: 68 when all four hints are main gear slots, 70 when one is an accessory (verified against week 449's live data) (file: Core/ScoreMath.cs WeeklyBase)
- /lfr opens the assistant window, /lfr refresh re-downloads the crowd data, /lfr changelog shows what's new (file: Plugin.cs OnCommand)
- Settings: auto-open with the Fashion Report window, owned-only candidate filter (on by default), candidates-per-slot limit (file: Configuration.cs, ConfigWindow.cs)

- Item candidates come from xivstats.com's crowdsourced database and exact weekly dyes from fashionreportxiv.com; both are cached locally and the plugin degrades gracefully to whatever loaded last when a fetch fails (file: Core/RemoteDataSource.cs)
- The predictor is offline-verified against week 449's published results: base 70, easy100 = the four gold items, easy80 = Brand-new Gloves + Abyssal Blue on the head slot (file: tests/LazyFashionReport.Harness)
- v1 does not change gear, apply dyes or submit anything: it only reads and advises (file: Plugin.cs)","RepoUrl":"https://github.com/dajoey/lalalazy/tree/main/src/LazyFashionReport","ApplicableVersion":"any","DalamudApiLevel":15,"IsHide":false,"IsTestingExclusive":true,"DownloadLinkInstall":"https://raw.githubusercontent.com/dajoey/lalalazy/main/plugins/LazyFashionReport/latest/latest.zip","DownloadLinkUpdate":"https://raw.githubusercontent.com/dajoey/lalalazy/main/plugins/LazyFashionReport/latest/latest.zip","DownloadLinkTesting":"https://raw.githubusercontent.com/dajoey/lalalazy/main/plugins/LazyFashionReport/testing/testing.zip","Tags":["fashion report","gold saucer","mgp","glamour","dye","lazy"],"CategoryTags":["utility"],"IconUrl":"https://raw.githubusercontent.com/dajoey/lalalazy/main/LalaImages/lazyfashionreport-icon.png","ImageUrls":[""],"DownloadCount":0,"LastUpdate":"0","_SourceId":"dajoey-lalalazy","_SourceName":"dajoey / lalalazy","_SourceUrl":"https://raw.githubusercontent.com/dajoey/lalalazy/main/pluginmaster.json"}

{"Author":"Akari","Name":"Market Helper","Punchline":"Undercut, list, gather and buy — market board automation end to end.","Description":"Market Helper is an all-in-one market board tool with three tabs:

UNDERCUT — Stand near a summoning bell and press Run. It walks every retainer on the bell and undercuts each listed item to the lowest price. HQ/NQ handling, own-retainer protection, per-item overrides, and price memory within a run. Skips mannequin/display items (detected by the game's mannequin icon) so they're never touched or delisted.

LISTER — Build a list of items (hold CTRL and hover to quick-add, or search). Press Go and it walks the bell and lists them all, pricing each at the most common market price (ignoring lone troll/outlier listings) minus your undercut. Prices against your world, data center, or whole region. Handles the 20-item-per-retainer cap by rolling extra items to the next retainer. Includes a no-touch dry-run preview.

FLIPPER — Search any marketable item and compare prices across Japan, America, Europe and Materia via Universalis. Top 10 listings per region, best cross-region flip, and seller/buyer tax modeling.

BUYER — Build a shopping list with a per-item quantity and a hard max price. Import a MakePlace furniture list or build a list by hand, choose your scope — my world, my data center, my whole region, or a custom set of data centers — and press SCAN to sweep it via Universalis and see, per item, where the cheapest listings are and how many are available under your cap. Press SEND and it hops world to world with Lifestream, opens a market board, and buys everything at or under your price. Dry run is on by default so you can prove the route without spending a gil, and every purchase is verified against the game's own confirmation dialog before it's accepted.

Open with /markethelp, /market, /mh, or /undercut.","InternalName":"MarketHelper","AssemblyVersion":"1.17.2.0","TestingAssemblyVersion":"1.17.2.0","RepoUrl":"https://github.com/dexcss/MarketHelper","ApplicableVersion":"any","DalamudApiLevel":15,"Tags":["market","retainer","undercut","marketboard","price","flip","universalis","lister"],"CategoryTags":["Utility"],"IconUrl":"https://raw.githubusercontent.com/dexcss/MarketHelper/main/images/icon.png","DownloadLinkInstall":"https://github.com/dexcss/MarketHelper/releases/latest/download/MarketHelper.zip","DownloadLinkUpdate":"https://github.com/dexcss/MarketHelper/releases/latest/download/MarketHelper.zip","DownloadLinkTesting":"https://github.com/dexcss/MarketHelper/releases/latest/download/MarketHelper.zip","IsHide":false,"IsTestingExclusive":false,"_SourceId":"dexcss-dalamudplugins","_SourceName":"dexcss / DalamudPlugins","_SourceUrl":"https://raw.githubusercontent.com/dexcss/DalamudPlugins/main/repo.json"}
